changes.summary: reduce routing and running-publication tracker reads
changes.body:
Routing queries now select only `id` and `description` for closed pending-label
repair and open-request discovery. Status filters, AND-label matching and
unlimited selection remain. Closed repair finishes before fresh open discovery;
full fresh reads still govern publication, registration and late authority checks.
No cache, configuration, CLI flag or native import/flush policy changes.

This record also covers 5f8727d4 and 98d74de6, whose integration messages kept
their declarations only as quoted provenance. Running publication reuses
authority-checked snapshots for no-ops. A running-fact write precedes stdout
and refreshes authority before stdout eligibility; due writes still check
fresh native authority. The comments are independent history, not an atomic
pair or proof of liveness.

For fact-current running requests, cohorts of at most four sample owned stdout
metadata and share one fresh native batch read for due requests. All due rows
are authority-checked before independent writes start. Admitted writes drain
before further discovery, pass failure or sleep. Cancellation, finish and
failed/stopped reconciliation retain precedence. Cohorts recheck the captured
attempt, immutable receipt, owned process and finish evidence; lifecycle drift
gets one fresh serial fallback, while a changed same-ID receipt fails.

The batch gate is sampled, not atomic: native hydration, locks and auto-flush
can age rows, and later closure or authority edits can race historical comments.
It promises neither serial-gate freshness nor race-free cancellation or
deduplication. Failures retain request IDs and primary/secondary causes; a failed
write may have committed, so re-entry uses fresh evidence to suppress duplicates.
`observations.publish-running` and `observations.publish-running-stdout` record
entry into publication, including no-ops, not confirmed writes. Initial
publication and settlement's final flush are unchanged.

The polling and wake entries below retain their effects: 60-second quiet
scheduling, five-second known-work/wake/degraded-watch scheduling and a
30-second stdout throttle are not end-to-end freshness bounds.

adoption.text:
Install `bee`, `colony`, `colony-runtime`, `colony-worker`, `colony-watchdog` and
`busybee` together from the same source release. Matching Busy Bee is required
by the native workflow-outcome contract in 384b538f. Read the Bee, Colony and
Busy Bee changelogs, coordinate active work, then follow
`colony daemon restart --help` to restart through the native service manager with the same state/socket.
Detached workers survive; existing captured recipes remain unchanged.

changes.summary: derive execution completion from each workflow anchor
changes.body:
A driver follows its run's native outcome; a stage worker follows its own visit.
Successful stage execution is independent of the authored choice and later run
cancellation. Failed/cancelled anchors retain that disposition rather than
becoming successful requests; a pending stage under a terminal run fails visibly.

Add owning-host execution clearance for Busy Bee settlement, serialized with
claim/reservation/supervisor admission. Complete retained attempt evidence is
required; closed requests alone do not prove process exit. Missing history,
foreign/unbound hosts, live/unverified processes and marked manual launches
refuse clearance. This read neither starts the daemon nor stops workers.
breaking:
unmarked closed workflow anchors no longer imply successful
request completion. Inspect the reported native evidence; existing Bee request
outcome/resolution semantics are otherwise unchanged.

adoption.text:
keep Colony and its companion executables coherent with Bee and Busy
Bee, and coordinate active work before refreshing the upgraded daemon through
`colony daemon restart --help`. Preserve retained execution history; no workflow
backfill or blanket abandonment of historical runs is required.

changes.summary: use wake hints with a 60-second quiet fallback
changes.body:
The default quiet delay changes from five to 60 seconds after a pass,
only for unchanged stable-running or empty colonies. Known transitions,
waiting/retry work and degraded watches retain five-second polling.
Database/WAL and current-attempt publication hints shorten the deadline to
five seconds after the previous pass, or immediately if already elapsed.
Startup/recovery scans remain immediate after watcher setup. Watch failures
emit a diagnostic and restore five-second polling until wake or replacement.
Each scan still reconciles fresh native facts; lifecycle authority and native
import settings are unchanged.

The 60-second bound is a quiet scheduling delay, not an end-to-end stop or
finish guarantee. Missed hints, JSONL-only changes and unobserved worker exits
can add that delay plus in-flight/native/process work. JSONL ingestion still
requires the existing native import configuration; auto-import is not enabled
by this change. Stdout does not wake a scan. Its 30-second publication spacing
is a throttle, not a freshness bound: a throttled change can wait the remaining
throttle plus up to another 60-second quiet interval and processing time.
Settlement still flushes the final observation once it runs. Output silence
is not a live-health verdict.
breaking: Unchanged stable-running or empty colonies now use a 60-second quiet post-pass delay instead of five seconds. Neither this delay nor the 30-second stdout throttle guarantees observation freshness or end-to-end completion.

adoption.text:
Upgrade the matching Colony companions together (`bee`, `colony`,
`colony-runtime`, `colony-worker`, `colony-watchdog`), then deliberately restart
each affected daemon with `colony daemon restart --json`, retaining its existing
state/socket selection. Read `colony daemon restart --help` for selection and
recovery. Detached workers survive the restart. Consumers relying on five-second
quiet polling or 30-second observation freshness must allow the delays above.

changes.summary: reduce tracker reads while polling running bees
changes.body:
Colony uses fewer native tracker commands by batching retained request
reads, reusing same-phase detail for unchanged observations, and limiting
preparation reads to waiting requests.
This optimization alone did not change polling cadence; 4d979791 subsequently
introduced the quiet-delay policy described above. Claims, observation writes
and settlement still check current native facts.

Required for an already-running daemon: after upgrading, run
`colony daemon restart --json` with the same state/socket selection to load
the new runtime. Detached workers continue running. Read
`colony daemon restart --help` for restart prerequisites and recovery.

changes.summary: remove hourly reviews, assessments and inactivity drones
changes.body:
Remove automatic hourly work reviews, post-run assessments and inactivity
Drone reviews. Automatic Nurse audits remain removed. Retire the entire
`colony work-review` command group and `colony assessments`, including their
schemas and results. Remove `auto_work_reviews`, `inactivity_drone` and
`post_run_drone` configuration and the public policy fields `autoWorkReviews`,
`inactivityDrone` and `postRunDrone`; `auto_nurse` remains unsupported.

Ordinary scheduling, capacity, task claims, retries, settlement, stdout
observations and process ownership checks remain. The supervisor still handles
owned execution stops; only auxiliary inspector deadlines are removed.

Existing private rows and artifacts are not automatically deleted or migrated.
Any historical cleanup requires a separately coordinated operation that
preserves active requests, task state and process ownership.
breaking: Hourly work reviews, post-run assessments and inactivity Drone reviews are removed, along with `colony work-review`, `colony assessments` and their configuration/result fields. Removed configuration keys are rejected.

adoption.text:
remove `auto_work_reviews`, `inactivity_drone`, `post_run_drone` and
any remaining `auto_nurse` keys from consuming repositories' canonical
`.hive/bees.toml` before loading configuration. Update consumers of the retired
commands, result schemas and public policy fields. Install matching Bee,
Colony, colony-runtime, colony-worker and colony-watchdog executables together.
Coordinate active workers with the runtime owner before an authorized daemon
restart. Installing binaries alone does not update the running daemon.

changes.summary: allow native daemon startup from tmux on macOS
changes.body:
Colony can start and verify its daemon from tmux when the current user's
macOS GUI launchd domain is available. This fixes wake, add and daemon
restart failing because the caller reports a Background bootstrap manager
or cannot see the service in its implicit launchd list.

Optional: after upgrading, retry `colony wake` from tmux with the same
repository, tracker and server selection. Native macOS startup still
requires the user's GUI launchd domain.

changes.summary: remove automatic nurse audits and control
changes.body:
Colony no longer schedules or reconciles nurse audit batches, advances their
coverage, or supplies current-topic snapshots to post-run drones. The
`auto_nurse` configuration key and `autoNurse` policy output are removed.
Post-run assessments and explicit nurse advice remain available. Retained
assessment reports and native audit, response and topic records remain readable;
the removed automation no longer writes health-control or topic records.

Required: remove top-level `auto_nurse` from canonical `.hive/bees.toml` before
running the new binaries or resetting policy. Install the matching Bee/Colony
executables together, then follow `colony daemon restart --help` and
`colony config reset --help` for the selected server and repository. Preserve
the tracker and retained state. Consumers of policy JSON must stop expecting
`autoNurse`.
breaking: remove automatic nurse audits and control

changes.summary: explicitly replace a retained daemon during unfinished restart
changes.body:
`colony daemon restart --replace-retained` selects one additional replacement
within an unfinished restart. Admission verifies the recorded daemon's endpoint,
lifetime, live process fingerprint and independent native ownership. The original
receipt evidence stays intact; `continuation` records the new leg and its effects.
A lost stop response can complete through a matched handoff and verified exit.
Final recovery protects original and intervening attempts without duplicate live
executions.

Retries resume saved phases. Uncertain stop/start calls are observed without
resubmission, so an interruption between saving intent and making its call can
remain incomplete and require diagnosis. Once the new daemon is observed,
retries finish its recovery in place. Failure JSON identifies request phases and
the retained continuation phase when available.

Optional: after updating the Colony executables together, read
`colony daemon restart --help` before selecting `--replace-retained` for an
unfinished restart. Keep the original state/socket and retained receipts.
Ordinary retries retain their existing in-place finalization behavior.

changes.summary: resume interrupted restarts through delayed repository recovery
changes.body:
`colony daemon restart` now polls repository recovery with a 10-minute deadline.
Recovery probes return promptly so other daemon commands can proceed while
scheduling passes finish. Connection and verification failures still fail the
operation and retain confirmed effects.

Retrying an unfinished restart with a recorded replacement resumes verification
of that matching, independently owned daemon against the original registration
and attempt manifest, without stopping or starting it again. An unavailable,
mismatched or unowned replacement is refused before its receipt changes.

Required: build and install the Colony CLI and its companion executables from
the same revision. To finish an interrupted restart, rerun
`colony daemon restart --json` with the original state/socket selection and
retain the restart and handoff receipts until verification succeeds.
breaking:
the daemon's `recover` request can now return `kind: recovering`
instead of waiting for `kind: status`. Protocol callers must poll until status,
check the daemon identity and selected endpoint on every response, then verify
recovery. A pending response does not establish successful recovery.

changes.summary: add opt-in hourly reviews of blocked and stranded work
changes.body:
The optional `auto_work_reviews` policy submits separate ordinary workflows for
native blocked tasks and stranded managed in-progress work. Fresh stable-blocker
receipts and empty candidate sets avoid drone launches. Native control retains
independent clocks, outstanding submissions and one recovery allowance per
request lineage across restarts.

Use `colony work-review --help` for preflight, retained control, diagnosis records
and bounded recovery, and `colony work-review --schema` for typed payloads. Recovery uses public Bee
retry with the original run/stage and execution directory; a submitted replacement
is not completed work.

Cancelled requests remain diagnosable without continuation authority. Recovering
a cancelled request requires incident-linked native human direction, preserving the actual recorder
and exact evidence references. The workflow assesses that direction; code checks
references and freshness without inferring permission from prose. Public Busy Bee
inspection validates the saved assignment in its original checkout before recovery
effects, with checkpoint and definition stamps rechecked. Missing or unsupported
saved state remains deferred. Colony also matches native and captured request
identity/task links alongside fresh stopped-process proof. These inspections do
not prove every future workflow path.

Uncertain effects remain visible and prevent blind resubmission. Hive's checked-in
policy opts this repository in with a dedicated control parent; live activation
still requires the deliberate policy reload.

Required after upgrading: refresh the Colony companion executables together and
follow `colony daemon restart --help` for the selected state/socket before querying
an active daemon's policy with the upgraded CLI.

Optional: enable reviews for a selected repository.

Required when enabling: prepare both workflow definitions and their dependencies
in the canonical checkout, and provision a dedicated ongoing
control parent that is an ordinary work bead. Inspect both preflight branches before adding
`auto_work_reviews = { kind = "drone", parent = "<review scope>" }`. Follow
`colony wake --help` or `colony config reset --help` for policy reload. Preserve the selected tracker,
state and existing control notes. Omission leaves automatic reviews disabled.

changes.summary: clarify role and task instruction placement
changes.body:
The bundled configuration guide assigns remit, judgement, authority limits
and professional result requirements to `system_prompt`; workflows own task
sequence, and input and stage briefs carry scope and acceptance. The same
role can serve different workflows. Optional prompt direction does not
change the assignment.

Optional: apply this distinction when authoring custom kinds and prompts;
no configuration schema or runtime policy change is required.

changes.summary: wait five seconds between reconciliation passes
changes.body:
Awake colonies now wait five seconds, rather than one, after each reconciliation
pass to reduce background polling overhead. Initial reconciliation still starts
immediately and passes remain serial.

Required: restart the Colony daemon after installing the updated executables to
apply the new delay to an already-running daemon.

changes.summary: schedule cumulative nurse audits after 25 new reports
changes.body:
Automatic audits freeze the oldest 25 unaudited completed reports and retain
failed-assessment gaps. Colony advances coverage only after the nurse workflow,
current request, authored response, native receipt and required investigations
have completed. Failed or uncertain delivery keeps the same batch outstanding.
Later drones receive bounded provisional topic snapshots within their existing
scope and deadline; health-scope requests are excluded from assessments.

Required for this Hive checkout: after installing the integrated Bee/Colony
artifacts, follow `colony daemon restart --help` for the selected server and
`colony wake --help` to load the committed policy. The configured ongoing health
parent is `hv-abym3l`; keep its machine notes intact and leave it open. Verify
`colony config show` reports the intended `autoNurse` selection. Activation has
no historical backfill; in-flight assessments count when they finish.

Optional for other repositories: provision an ordinary ongoing health parent
and configured nurse kind/formula, then set top-level
`auto_nurse = { kind = "nurse", parent = "<ordinary health scope>" }` before
reloading policy. Omission disables new batches. Baseline, backlog and any
active audit survive disable/re-enable; retain the same parent, kind, tracker,
host and state. See the Colony guide's automatic-nurse section for recovery.

changes.summary: launch drivers with compact workflow reading guidance
changes.body:
New driver execution attempts receive explicit native run/task brief reads
and a pointer to Busy Bee's instruction expansion help. Routine status
checks use compact run views; relevant scope, state or authority changes
trigger a fresh native brief read.

No configuration change is required. Claim ownership, worker waiting,
result delivery and Busy Bee's completion authority are unchanged.

changes.summary: read group ownership independently of writer history
changes.body:
Group observation and cleanup read the recorded supervisor identity and token without
validating unused writer fields. Retained attempt and assessment artifacts with discarded
process-history fields no longer block cleanup. Token, supervisor lifetime and process-group
checks remain in force; new ownership writes remain unchanged.

Required: drain or stop old attempts with the old Colony runtime before replacing binaries.
Install all matching Colony companion executables, then restart the daemon and resume
unfinished work. Old supervisors keep their scan loops until stopped.

adoption.text: Drain or stop old attempts with the old Colony runtime before replacing binaries. Install all matching Colony companion executables, then restart the daemon and resume unfinished work. Old supervisors keep their scan loops until stopped.

changes.summary: replace recurring process scans with owned-group supervision
changes.body:
Managed executions now observe their child handle without continuous process-table scans or
descendant-history rewrites. Cancellation sends TERM to the verified supervisor process group,
allows one second for exit, then sends KILL if needed and waits up to five seconds for
confirmation. Cleanup fails visibly if the group remains. Processes that detach or create
separate groups are outside managed cleanup.

Required: drain or stop old attempts with the old Colony runtime before upgrading, install all
matching Colony companion binaries, then restart the daemon and resume unfinished work.
Restarting the daemon alone leaves old supervisors and their scan loops alive.
breaking: replace recurring process scans with owned-group supervision

matching Colony companion binaries, then restart the daemon and resume unfinished work.
Restarting the daemon alone leaves old supervisors and their scan loops alive.

changes.summary: submit observer reports through Bee system protocols
changes.body:
Generated inactivity and post-run assessment instructions use `bee system report`
and `bee system assess`. The assessment wrapper owns its submission protocol and
constraints; the configured role supplies assessment guidance. Foreground operation
remains `colony daemon serve`.

Required: upgrade Colony with the matching Bee executable and update custom
observer prompts that embed the former report or assess command paths.

adoption.text:
upgrade Colony with the matching Bee executable and update custom
observer prompts that embed the former report or assess command paths.

changes.summary: bound request explanations to relevant runtime evidence
changes.body:
`colony explain` reads the selected checkpoint and complete attempt history.
Capacity keeps one kind/bucket entry per retained starting/running attempt
bound by its request checkpoint to the daemon's host. Unrelated terminal
history and policy revisions are excluded; `colony inspect` and `status`
retain their existing output.

Required: update Colony and its companion executables together, coordinate
active work, and refresh any running daemon. Follow
`colony daemon restart --help`, preserving the selected state/socket.
An older daemon cannot handle `inspect-request`; explain reports unavailable
runtime evidence without falling back to full inspection.

BREAKING CHANGE: `colony explain --json` omits
`runtime.result.value.colony.attempts`. Use `runtime.result.value.attempts`
for the selected request's complete history, or `colony inspect` for
repository-wide history. The new socket command requires an updated daemon.
breaking:
`colony explain --json` omits
`runtime.result.value.colony.attempts`. Use `runtime.result.value.attempts`
for the selected request's complete history, or `colony inspect` for
repository-wide history. The new socket command requires an updated daemon.

changes.summary: expose execution history without contacting the daemon
changes.body:
Run `colony changelog` to read recorded execution changes offline. Colony's
history also covers its runtime, worker and watchdog companion executables.

changes.summary: The shared daemon supports native launchd/systemd supervision and recovers verified surviving executions after restart.
